A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WSI-LLaVA and WSI-Bench. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support comparison, including matching retained content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original WSI-Bench evaluations, encoder and training-stage ablations, and qualitative model comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds external evaluations, detailed morphological analyses, and comparisons between automated metrics and medical experts.

M1.justification: The architecture and three-stage framework remain. However, v1 Appendix 4.2 trains the WSI and text encoders in stage one, whereas v3 Appendix 5.2 freezes both and trains only an MLP; v3 Figure 4 still depicts encoder training. This conflict prevents reliably distinguishing a substantive procedure change from inconsistent documentation. The stage-three appendix revision aligns it with training already described in v1's main text.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on WSI-VQA, SlideBench-VQA (BCNB), and CPTAC-NSCLC, substantially extending coverage beyond WSI-Bench (Section 5.4). WSI-Bench retains its 30 cancer types and 11 tasks; presenting report generation as a fourth capability reorganizes existing coverage.

E2.justification: SlideChat becomes an evaluated comparator in v3 Table 6. The main VQA example adds WSI-VQA, while the revised metric-comparison example removes MI-Gen. Appendix Table 3 also compares alternative LLM judges. The principal WSI-Bench comparator sets in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces zero-shot external testing, specified question exclusions, a binary classification prompt for 1,091 CPTAC slides, and a five-expert metric-validation protocol. The reported dataset review changes from reviewing every VQA pair to sampling 10% of open-ended and 5% of closed-ended pairs. These are substantive protocol additions and revisions, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-dataset generalization tests, expert validation and alternative-judge analysis of WSI metrics, and separate infiltration, tissue, and cellular morphology results in Figure 5. Main-text qualitative cases are also added or replaced. The original encoder and training-stage ablations remain, merged into Appendix Table 2 rather than constituting new ablation experiments.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports human–automated Pearson correlations of 0.87 and 0.82 and inter-rater Cohen's kappa of 0.78 in its metric-validation study. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-training-run uncertainty for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: v3 adds external, expert-validation, and detailed morphology results. Table 3 revises WSI-LLaVA BLEU-1/ROUGE-L from 0.3531/0.2626 to 0.480/0.490 and Quilt-LLaVA BLEU-1 from 0.3343 to 0.474, reversing the language-metric ranking; WSI-LLaVA's WSI-Precision/Relevance remain 0.380/0.429. These are revised reported results, not an established same-setting improvement. The merged ablation table also replaces v1 Table 7's 0.448/0.676 full-model precision/average with 0.488/0.680, matching v1 Table 4.

T1.justification: The claim-based metric definitions, four scoring levels, and averaging formula are retained. The new workflow illustration and empirical validation introduce no new mathematical definition, theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate explainability and morphology-supported diagnostic reasoning to central contributions. v1's explicit claim of establishing a morphology–diagnostic accuracy correlation is replaced by this emphasis and claims of superiority on both internal and external datasets.

C2.justification: The new supplementary Discussion attributes external generalization to transferable morphological knowledge and extends implications to different institutions and patient populations. Metric validation adds interpretations of automated scoring conservatism and disagreement on subtle morphology or clinical context. The earlier report-generation trade-off between language metrics and clinical accuracy is replaced by an all-metrics superiority interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code/data release statement and repository link, stage-two and stage-three global batch sizes of 256 and 128, and the within-cancer testing allocation of 2% with a two-slide minimum. It revises training documentation and omits the earlier hard-negative sampling specification. Most architecture details, hyperparameters, and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Related Work replaces the detailed patch-level model discussion with a pathology VQA benchmark subsection and reframes SlideChat comparisons around explanations and morphological reasoning. Added references include PathVQA, EAGLE, WSI-Agents, and medical-LLM studies; the previous UNI and QuiltNet discussions disappear. This substantially changes research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, task descriptions, and method exposition undergo substantial rewriting. Baseline descriptions merge into quantitative evaluation, detailed ablations move to the supplement, and a supplementary Discussion is introduced. Most later appendix prompts and examples retain their wording.

P2.justification: v3 adds an explanatory model comparison, morphology radar plot, external-results table, train/test distribution plots, metric workflow, and judge-comparison table. It merges and relocates the ablation tables and substantially revises the main qualitative and metric-comparison displays. Existing appendix prompt figures are retained.

improvement.justification: External evaluations and expert validation address important gaps in v1, while added implementation and access information improves documentation. However, v3's stage-one instructions conflict with Figure 4, its validation study cites 124,011 open-ended test responses without reconciling them with the 2,838 test questions reported elsewhere, and substantial Table 3 score revisions lack an explanation. These ambiguities affect the method and new supporting evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
